description: Why every Ajisai evaluation is finite, as data rather than as a sentence. Ajisai has no recursion and no unbounded loop, so this is a real property of the language and not a budget the host happens to enforce — but it is a property with an exact shape, and that shape is what this file states: the places evaluation descends into more evaluation, what strictly decreases at each one, and the two rules the whole argument rests on — no Word reaches itself through the dictionary, and no block built from data runs inside another.
claim: Every evaluation of a well-formed Ajisai program halts. The ceilings of LANG.MACHINE.LIMITS bound what a run may cost; none of them decides whether it ends.

consequence.totality: Ajisai is a total language: it is not Turing-complete, and that is a deliberate trade rather than an omission.
consequence.cost: There is no unbounded iteration. A computation that must run until it converges, rather than once per element of a collection that already exists, cannot be written — it has to be re-expressed over a finite Vector the program builds first.
consequence.benefit: A denotational reading of Ajisai needs no domain theory: with no divergence there is no bottom to model, no continuity obligation and no least-fixed-point construction, so the semantic function is an ordinary recursive function on finite structures.
consequence.selfInterpretation: A total language cannot define an interpreter for itself, so Ajisai cannot be its own metalanguage. This is also why the pre-execution check of LANG.CONTRACT.CHECK is necessarily conservative and partial rather than merely cautious.

invariant.statement: A Word runs only when a Symbol naming it is written in source. There is no way to compute a call: no Word turns text into a Symbol, and a String is not code (LANG.SOURCE.CODE), so the code operand of the higher-order Words is a Vector and nothing else.
invariant.whyItMatters: The acyclicity checks read the Symbols a body or a bound value holds. They are sound only if every call it can make is visible to them as a Symbol. A call reachable some other way would not be in the reference graph at all, and the graph's acyclicity would say nothing about whether that call returns.
invariant.history: Until this was fixed, the higher-order Words also accepted a String naming a Word as their code operand. The name could be computed, so it appeared in no token for the check to read: `[ [ 1 ] [ 'J' 'W' ] JOIN MAP ] 'JW' DEF` was accepted and then recursed until the native depth guard fired. Termination there was decided by a ceiling, which is exactly what the claim above says it never is.

refused.note: A String, even one naming a real Word, is not a code operand.
The computed-name case, which no DEF-time check could ever have caught.

accepted.note: The Vector spelling, which names DBL with a Symbol the acyclicity check reads.

acyclicity.statement: The reference graph the Symbols of a program can reach is acyclic. DEF refuses a definition whose body names the Word being defined, directly or through any chain of other User Words, however that name is reached — a Symbol inside a Record or other value the body carries whole included. BIND refuses a value that names its own binding, directly or through other bindings the frame can see, because a binding is looked up when its Vector runs and would otherwise call itself with no Word in between.
acyclicity.consequence: A chain of Word calls is therefore shorter than the number of User Words, so it cannot be infinite. The binding check is not what bounds a chain of bound values — a bound value run in a frame other than the one that wrote it is built from data, and `stratification` bounds that — but it refuses a binding cycle when the binding is made, which is earlier and plainer than the run that would reach it.

refused.source:
[ B ] 'A' DEF
[ C ] 'B' DEF
[ A ] 'C' DEF

refused.note: Reached only through a nested block, which LANG.SOURCE.FRAME says still counts as a reference even though nothing there evaluates it.
A forward reference to a Word that does not exist yet: the cycle closes at the second DEF, which is where it is caught. Definition order does not matter.

refused.source: [ 'k' ] [ [ W ] ] RECORD 1 COLLECT [ 'k' GET EXEC ] CONCAT 'W' DEF
refused.note: The name is held inside a Record the body carries whole, where no top-level Symbol shows it. The check reads every Symbol the body holds, not only the ones written at its top level.
A binding whose value runs its own name. No Word is defined, so a check that read only definitions would miss it.

refused.source:
[ G EXEC ] 'F' BIND
[ F EXEC ] 'G' BIND
refused.note: Indirect, through another binding: the cycle closes at the second BIND.
Destructuring cannot close a cycle between its own parts: the names bound together count as bound already.

accepted.source:
[ 1 ] 'W1' DEF
[ W1 ] 'W2' DEF
[ W2 ] 'W3' DEF
W3
accepted.note: An acyclic chain. Completeness matters as much as soundness: a check that refused this would make the language smaller, not safer.

accepted.source:
[ 1 ] 'F' BIND
[ F EXEC F EXEC ADD ] 'G' BIND
G EXEC
accepted.note: A binding that runs another binding, twice, with no cycle.

stratification.statement: A block run by EXEC, MAP, FILTER, FOLD or SCAN is written when it equals a Vector literal of the code running it, or a Vector nested inside one, or names no Word; otherwise it is built from data. A block built from data is refused while another block built from data is running.
stratification.why: The dictionary's acyclicity bounds every call made by name, but a block can be taken apart and rebuilt from data — `1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET` makes two copies of one — and a copy names nothing that a reference graph could see. A written block is part of the code that runs it, so it is smaller; a block built from data can be as large as anything, including the block running it. Allowing one such run per chain of descents and no more is what puts it under a measure.
stratification.history: Until 1.0.0-beta.3 nothing enforced this. `[ 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC EXEC ] 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC EXEC` ran a copy of itself until the callDepth ceiling stopped it at 257 frames, and a block that chose its own base case with SELECT ran a countdown that ended on its own: the claim below was false, and a ceiling decided termination.

refused.source: [ 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC EXEC ] 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC EXEC
refused.note: Self-application with no Word and no binding: the written block runs, its copy is built from data, and the copy's copy is the second one.

refused.source: [ 'N' BIND N PRINT 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC N 1 SUB 3 COLLECT [ 0 2 1 ] GET [ EXEC EXEC ] [ 'done' ] N 0 GT SELECT EXEC ] 3 [ 'N' BIND N PRINT 1 COLLECT [ 0 0 ] GET EXEC N 1 SUB 3 COLLECT [ 0 2 1 ] GET [ EXEC EXEC ] [ 'done' ] N 0 GT SELECT EXEC ] EXEC
refused.note: A recursion with a base case chosen by SELECT, which ended on its own before this rule: a terminating recursion is refused as surely as a divergent one, because the rule reads where a block stands and not what it would do.

refused.source: [ 'F' BIND F F EXEC ] 'RUN' DEF [ RUN ] RUN
refused.note: Through a User Word: RUN's body runs its operand, which is built from data, and that operand calls RUN again.

refused.source:
[ 1 ] 'A0' BIND
[ A0 EXEC ] 'A1' BIND
[ A1 EXEC ] 'A2' BIND
[ A2 EXEC ] 'A3' BIND
A3 EXEC
refused.note: The price, not a recursion: each block is bound in the top frame and run from inside the next, so A2 is built from data inside A3 and A1 inside A2 — the second run is refused, though the chain would end. Write such a chain as Words, which run no block.

accepted.note: A block bound and run in the frame that wrote it is written there.

accepted.source: [ [ 1 2 ] [ [ 3 ] [ 1 ADD ] MAP 0 GET ADD ] MAP ] EXEC
accepted.note: Blocks written inside blocks run at any depth.

accepted.source: [ 'F' BIND 1 F EXEC ] 'APPLY' DEF [ 2 ADD ] APPLY
accepted.note: One block built from data, run by a Word that was handed it.
SELECT chooses between two written blocks, and the chosen one is still written: a branch costs nothing new.

measure.note: Lexicographic, outermost component first. Every descent below strictly decreases one component and increases none before it, so no descent chain is infinite; each frame descends finitely often, since its code is finite and a walk visits a collection that already exists, so the whole evaluation is finite.

components.description: How many runs of a block built from data the chain may still make: one before any, none after. Nothing raises it, because a second run while one is active is refused (`stratification`).

The length of the longest chain of User Word references leaving the code being evaluated: the rank of the Word whose body it is part of, or one more than the dictionary's longest chain for the program and for a block built from data. Finite because the reference graph is acyclic and the dictionary is finite.
The size of the code being evaluated. A written block equals part of the code running it, so it is strictly smaller; finite because a Vector is finite and cannot contain itself.
How many elements of the collection being walked are still unvisited. The collection is already materialized when the walk begins, so this is a finite number that falls by one per step.

recursionSites.descendsInto: the body of the named Word
recursionSites.why: The callee's longest outgoing reference chain is shorter than that of the code calling it, because the graph is acyclic, and the call runs no block, so dataBlockRuns is unchanged.

recursionSites.descendsInto: a block built from data, when EXEC or a higher-order Word runs it
recursionSites.why: It is the only run of a block built from data on its chain: a second one is refused. Inside it dictionaryRank and codeSize start again from the block's own, which is why dataBlockRuns comes first.
recursionSites.witness:
[ [ 1 ] EXEC ] 'F' BIND
[ F EXEC ] 'G' BIND
G EXEC

recursionSites.descendsInto: the Vector operand, read as code, when it is written
recursionSites.why: A written operand equals a Vector literal of the code running EXEC, or one nested inside it, so the code it runs is strictly part of the code that ran it. An operand built from data is the dataBuiltBlock site.

recursionSites.descendsInto: the code block, once per element
recursionSites.why: The collection is finite and already materialized, so the block runs a fixed number of times; each run descends as EXEC's does, into a written block or the dataBuiltBlock site.

recursionSites.descendsInto: the code block, once per element
the code block, once per element
recursionSites.why: As MAP. The accumulator changes value but adds no descent of its own.

recursionSites.descendsInto: the code block, once per element
recursionSites.why: As FOLD — the same walk over the same materialized collection. Keeping every accumulator rather than only the last one adds a value to the answer, not a descent.

ceilings.note: LANG.MACHINE.LIMITS' ceilings bound cost. None of them is what makes a program end, and a program that needs one to stop is a bug in this argument, not a program the language accepts. The witnesses above are run under the default profile and must all finish without reaching any ceiling.
